name: Tesa/IPA Protocol
lead: The Tesa/IPA protocol is a term used in peptide and body-composition circles for pairing two injectable growth-hormone-axis peptides, tesamorelin and ipamorelin, with the aim of leaner, more defined physiques. The two are different substances: tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), while ipamorelin is a pentapeptide that acts on the ghrelin (growth hormone secretagogue) receptor. [1][2]

The looks chain people describe is: more growth hormone release, raising IGF-1, lowering body fat (particularly around the abdomen) and supporting lean mass, which gives a sharper waist and more visible muscle. Tesamorelin's recognised effect in its approved use is lipolysis, the breakdown of fat. [1]

Tesamorelin is a prescription drug sold by Theratechnologies as Egrifta, first approved in 2010 for HIV-associated lipodystrophy. [1] Ipamorelin was developed by Novo Nordisk, later tested by Helsinn Therapeutics for postoperative ileus, where development stopped because of lack of efficacy; it is not an approved drug and is commonly sold as a research peptide. [2]

Proponents pair the two because they release growth hormone through different receptors. No published trial has tested the combination in humans. On T Nation, one user reported that IGF-1 rose above 300 on tesamorelin plus ipamorelin but barely moved on a CJC/ipamorelin pairing, and described the former as the option they would return to. [3]

Unapproved; sold as a research peptide [2]

paras: Tesamorelin consists of the full 44 amino acids of human GHRH with a trans-3-hexenoic acid group added, which makes it more potent and more resistant to breakdown than natural GHRH. It stimulates the body's own growth hormone release, raising IGF-1, and its main effect on body fat is lipolysis. [1]

Reported adverse effects include injection-site redness and itching, peripheral edema, diarrhea and joint or limb pain; it may cause glucose intolerance and raise type 2 diabetes risk, and it is contraindicated in pregnancy and in patients with hypothalamic-pituitary disruption. [1]

Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide derived from GHRP-1 that selectively agonises the ghrelin receptor. It raises plasma growth hormone in animals and humans and, unlike GHRP-2 and GHRP-6, is reported not to stimulate ACTH or cortisol. Its elimination half-life is about two hours. [2]
Helsinn's phase II program for postoperative ileus stopped because of lack of efficacy. It appears among WADA-prohibited substances and has been used by athletes as a performance-enhancing drug. [2]

Proponents describe the two peptides as complementary: a GHRH analogue amplifies the pituitary's growth-hormone pulses, while a ghrelin-receptor agonist triggers a release through a second pathway. Ipamorelin is reported to raise growth hormone without stimulating ACTH or cortisol, which proponents cite as a reason it is chosen over other secretagogues. [2]

Forum users commonly track IGF-1 blood tests as their marker of response. In a T Nation thread on growth hormone, one poster compared tesamorelin/ipamorelin with CJC/ipamorelin by IGF-1 values and noted tesamorelin-based stacks cost more than CJC-based ones while remaining cheaper than pharmaceutical growth hormone. [3]

On looksmax.org, ipamorelin is more often discussed in combination with CJC-1295 for height or general growth in younger users, and a thread asks whether tesamorelin interacts with a CJC-1295/ipamorelin regimen. [4][5]

No studies found. Tesamorelin has been studied for HIV-associated lipodystrophy, and ipamorelin in a postoperative ileus trial and a healthy-volunteer pharmacokinetic study, but not together and not for cosmetic purposes. [1][2] Ipamorelin has also been examined in rat studies of bone growth, which looksmax.org users cite in height discussions; these are animal research. [5]

No studies found. Tesamorelin has been studied for HIV-associated lipodystrophy, and ipamorelin in a postoperative ileus trial and a healthy-volunteer pharmacokinetic study, but not together and not for cosmetic purposes. [1][2]

timeline.event: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) first approved in the US for HIV-associated lipodystrophy. [1]

lore.intro: The combination is discussed in peptide-oriented body-composition circles as a fat-loss and growth-hormone stack, and ipamorelin more broadly appears in looksmax.org height and body-composition threads. [3][4][5]

claims.claim: Combining tesamorelin and ipamorelin gives a stronger or complementary growth-hormone release for fat loss
claims.believers: Proponents argue the two act on different receptors (GHRH and ghrelin) and so complement one another; one T Nation user reported higher IGF-1 on Tesa/Ipa than on CJC/Ipa. [3]
claims.experts: No published human study has tested the combination; tesamorelin's evidence is in HIV-associated lipodystrophy, and ipamorelin's clinical development was stopped for lack of efficacy in ileus. [1][2]

claims.claim: Ipamorelin can add height or bone growth in people with open growth plates
claims.believers: Looksmax.org users point to a rat study reporting longitudinal bone growth with ipamorelin and to related rat bone-mineral work. [5]
claims.experts: The cited work is animal research; no published human trial has tested ipamorelin for height. [2]

card.summary: A tesamorelin plus ipamorelin injectable peptide stack for fat loss; each part has some history, the combination has no trials.
card.note: Tesamorelin is Rx-only; ipamorelin is unapproved and WADA-prohibited.

quick.overview:
Tesa/IPA means using the prescription GHRH analogue tesamorelin together with the unapproved peptide ipamorelin, mainly for fat loss.

Tesamorelin is approved for HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Ipamorelin was abandoned in clinical development. No trial has tested the pair.
quick.mechanism: Tesamorelin mimics growth-hormone-releasing hormone; ipamorelin activates the ghrelin receptor. Both raise growth hormone and hence IGF-1.
quick.risks: Tesamorelin labelling-type effects include injection-site reactions, edema, joint pain and glucose intolerance. Ipamorelin is unapproved and appears on the WADA prohibited list.
